question.text: A Pre-emptive Right entitles an existing shareholder to:

answer.text: Maintain their percentage shareholding by participating pro-rata in future rounds of financing or stock option exercises
Receive dividends before common shareholders only
Vote with 2x voting power on all ordinary resolutions
Block the company from issuing any new debt securities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.3, the most common anti-dilution right is the 'pre-emptive right' — a shareholder's right to maintain their percentage shareholding by participating pro-rata and purchasing shares issued in future rounds or stock options exercised. It is a RIGHT, not an obligation. The Trap: Pre-emptive is about shareholding percentage, not dividend priority, voting multipliers, or debt veto. Cross-Exam Context: Pre-emptive right tested in Companies Act 2013 Section 62 on further issue of capital, cross-referenced in XIX-A and III-A. Manager's Pro-Tip: In follow-on rounds, LPs with pre-emptive rights either participate or waive in writing. Get waivers or participations lined up BEFORE the new investor's closing date — ambiguous status paralyzes the closing.
